Interpolation precedence: "1. Variables from your shell environment 2. Variables from a file set by --env-file 3. If --env-file is not set, variables from an .env file in the project directory". So up.sh takes .env's value only when the calling terminal does not already hold POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Rest verified (docker-compose.yml lab: PGPASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"; docker exec doc above).

issues.quote: reads it once from `.env` through the tool it runs
issues.text: Still unfixed from r1. Compose interpolation precedence puts "Variables from your shell environment" before the project .env file; if the terminal running up.sh already holds POSTGRES_PASSWORD, that value goes into the box. Stated unconditionally here, in claim 18 and in quiz q4 option b.
issues.fix: Replace with 'takes it from `.env` through the tool it runs (a value your terminal already holds under that name would win)'. Set claim 18 to its suggested_text. Optionally append to q4 option b: 'unless your terminal already holds one'.

issues.quote: because the script's lines are read and run by a program like `sh`; on the next line a second `sh` is started as its child
issues.text: env-demo.sh is run by bash (shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bash`; lab-run.sh runs `bash "$0"`), and /bin/sh in the box is busybox. "a second `sh`" implies the script itself runs in sh. Also the direct child on line 10 is `env`, which then runs `sh`.
issues.fix: Replace with 'because the script's lines are read and run by `bash`; on the next line `env` starts `sh` as a child of the script, with `-c '…'` as the words typed after its name'.

issues.quote: `${DONHANG_MISSING:-nothing}` supplies a fallback when nothing was handed in — the same idea as `??` in the sample
issues.text: `:-` also uses the fallback when the name was handed in with an empty value (in donhang-lab, `X= sh -c 'echo [${X:-nothing}]'` printed [nothing]; Compose doc: "value of VAR if set and non-empty, otherwise default"), while `??` keeps an empty string. "the same idea" is hedged, but "when nothing was handed in" is incomplete.
issues.fix: Replace 'supplies a fallback when nothing was handed in' with 'supplies a fallback when nothing (or an empty value) was handed in'.

issues.quote: A process is handed a copy of a set of name–value pairs when it starts, and reads configuration from that copy.
issues.text: Overgeneralises: section 3 and Connections say configuration also arrives through files and command-line words. As written the summary says configuration is read from the environment copy.
issues.fix: Replace 'and reads configuration from that copy' with 'and can read configuration from that copy'.

issues.quote: reads it once from `.env` through the tool it runs
issues.text: "The tool it runs" is never named or described, so I cannot tell what actually opens `.env` or why `docker-compose.yml` matters to it. I can still follow where the value ends up (the box's set), so this did not stop me.
issues.fix: Add a half-clause saying `scripts/up.sh` runs a tool that reads both `docker-compose.yml` and the `.env` beside it; naming the tool is not needed.

issues.quote: The box is given that one set when it is created, and every process the box is asked to start begins with a copy of it.
issues.text: Section 3 says every process carries a set, but the lab box was described only as "a closed-off corner of your machine with its own files and its own processes", not as a process. So "the box's set" is a new idea: I had to assume the box behaves like a parent process. I followed it, but only by guessing.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before this one saying the box keeps one set of pairs of its own, which it hands out like a parent to every process started inside it.

issues.quote: then creates the box with that value, under the name `docker-compose.yml` lists, in the box's set.
issues.text: I read this sentence twice: three trailing phrases (with that value / under the name … lists / in the box's set) make it hard to see that the value is stored under a name taken from `docker-compose.yml`.
issues.fix: Rewrite as two short clauses: 'then creates the box and puts the value into the box's set, under the name `docker-compose.yml` lists.'

issues.quote: `export` puts a name and a value into this run's own set, which is what it passes on to what it starts, and `printenv` prints one of them
issues.text: The paragraph after the output explains `export`, `printenv`, the script's own `sh`, the child `sh`, `-c`, and `env` in three long sentences. I re-read it twice, and at first looked for two separate script lines for the child `sh` and for `env`, although they are the same line.
issues.fix: Split the paragraph after the `printenv` sentence, and say once that the single `env … sh -c '…'` line both starts a child and hands it a different value.

issues.quote: These are the name it reads and the lines of its `Run()` method
issues.text: The C# block stops after the fourth `Console.WriteLine` with no closing brace, so I could not tell whether `Run()` prints more. Quiz q5 then speaks of "its four output lines"; I only trust that number because the quiz says so.
issues.fix: Add to the sentence before the block that these are all the lines `Run()` contains (or that it prints four lines).
